source_tokens.text: "Communicative Arithmetic is a synthetic cost model, not a hardware benchmark or direct evidence about human networks. Across 500 requests, fixed FP32 accepted 387 with 0.81156 ms mean latency and 0.000159251 mean error; semantic routing with cache accepted 494 with 1.29354 ms mean latency, 0.000348699 mean error, and 0.356 cache reuse; semantic routing without cache accepted 490 with 1.54258 ms mean latency. Cache reduced semantic mean latency by 16.14 percent relative to no cache, but semantic routing was slower than fixed FP32 in the baseline and had higher mean error. The sweep found semantic routing lower in mean latency in 2 of 16 cells, cached wins by mean in 34 of 81 crossover cells, robust cached wins in 10 of 72 extended cells, and robust cached wins in 6 of 30 far-distance cells. The result supports a conditional caching and coordination hypothesis, not a general claim that networked horsepower is superior."
